title: personal-llm-mini-tracker-rami-2026.json
content:
Experiment mini-sheet - personal tracker for quick inference bench notes

Columns: experiment_id | date | model | quant | batch_size | p50_latency_ms | p95_latency_ms | tokens_per_usd | notes | status

rows:
E1 | 2026-01-12 | redwood-open-3b | int8 | 1 | 52 | 120 | 1,200 | baseline single-token throughput; stable KV cache | done
E2 | 2026-01-20 | redwood-open-3b | int8 | 4 | 68 | 130 | 3,900 | small batch increases throughput but p95 worsens; try async batching | in_review
E3 | 2026-02-02 | redwood-open-3b | int8 + q4_0 | 1 | 45 | 110 | 1,500 | q4_0 reduced latency by ~13% in p50; check quality regression on promptset A | draft
E4 | 2026-02-18 | redwood-open-7b | int8 | 1 | 95 | 230 | 800 | 7b higher quality but cost/latency tradeoff; consider dynamic routing for short queries | draft
E5 | 2026-02-25 | redwood-open-3b | int8 | 8 | 140 | 360 | 6,800 | high batch gives best tokens/USD but p95 poor; investigate prefix caching warmup | draft

Quick notes / observations:
- KV cache warmup matters: run 10 warmup tokens before measuring p95; inconsistent if not warmed.
- For short prompt workloads (<64 tokens) prefer batch_size 1-4; above that, batching helps.
- q4_0 seems promising for small models; add targeted eval on customer prompts (ConvoSet-C).
- Latency variance correlates with GC pauses in the runner when memory pressure hits (see linked PR).
